name: Outlaw
description: A calm country singer in her fifties with an unhurried, self-possessed stage presence. Mature, sturdy, relaxed and hip-loaded with grounded staggered boots; never a narrow fashion pose or an exaggerated cowboy caricature. Her recognition cues are a broad perfectly level western-hat brim, long hair falling in hard bands beneath it, a western shoulder yoke, a loaded hip, and staggered boots, all readable without facial detail. She wears a turquoise western shirt with a clear shoulder yoke, dark trousers, a broad belt with a simple metal buckle, sturdy brown boots, and a plain broad-brim western hat. She holds one wireless handheld microphone loosely at hip height in her character-right hand; no cable, stand, firearm, lasso or weapon-like accessory. Her ready stance has weight settled into the rear hip, knees flexed, boots staggered, the free hand near the belt, and the character-right hand holding the microphone naturally at hip height. Palette, as base/shadow/highlight per material: dark #20232B / #101217 / #3A3E48; white #F1EEE5 / #BDB9AE / #FFFFFF; metal #6F747C / #34383E / #B5BAC0; turquoise #35C8B0 / #197867 / #70E4CF; brown #6C4329 / #352014 / #9B6945; skin #B97251 / #70422E / #DA9773; hair #59402D / #2A1E16 / #856548; hat #8A6B43 / #4B3924 / #B89764. Never draw: tilted or curved hat brim; cowboy caricature; sheriff badge; firearm or lasso; fringe overload; brand marks; aggressive draw stance; microphone cable, stand, or duplicate microphone; firearm, lasso, or weapon-like accessory. the cowboy had looks like: Color: A warm, earthy medium brown, somewhere between camel and milk chocolate. In close-ups it has a slightly olive, taupe tint. Texture: Matte felt with a soft, velvety nap. Up close you can see fine fibers and a few flecks, so it looks handmade rather than slick. Crown: Tall, with a classic cattleman shape: a long crease down the center and two pinches in the front. It narrows a bit toward the top. Brim: Wide and flat at the front and back, turned up at the sides into a gentle taco-like curve. The edge is raw-cut, with no binding. Band: A thin dark-brown leather strap wraps around the base of the crown. It's tied in a simple knot at one side, and the two ends hang down loose onto the brim. The leather looks rugged, with some scuffing.

animations.dance: Relaxed country dance loop: trade weight between staggered boots with an unhurried hip shift, let the long banded hair and level hat brim follow, then return to the rear-hip opening stance. microphone does not need to be pointed at face and microphone arm is free to move
animations.sing: Country vocal loop: keep weight loaded into the rear hip, lift the microphone in the character-right hand from hip height for a sustained line, make one free-hand belt-side gesture, then settle back into the relaxed stance. The mouth must visibly open and change shape across the loop so she unmistakably reads as singing.
animations.flinch: Brief room-sound surprise: shoulders and long hair react while the hat brim stays level, the microphone remains in the character-right hand, then she restores her calm hip-loaded stance. No opponent or contact.
animations.guard: One-shot stage self-protection: brace through the staggered boots, draw the free arm across the torso, keep the microphone in the character-right hand low and secure, then hold a steady final pose. Not combat.
animations.entrance: One-shot entrance: walk in with slow purposeful boot steps, level hat brim and western yoke clear, acknowledge the room with the free hand, then settle into the relaxed rear-hip stance.
animations.victory: One-shot performance finish: tip the level hat brim only with a small respectful gesture while lifting the free hand, then hold a calm proud pose with the microphone at the hip.
animations.ko: Non-contact performance defeat: she stays on her feet while the loaded hip levels out and the unhurried composure goes — her head hangs low with the chin toward her chest so the broad western-hat brim tips forward and shades her face while staying broad and readable. The microphone hangs at hip height in her character-right hand and she holds a standing, visibly dejected finish with her boots staggered and planted. She remains standing in every frame — no kneeling, crouching, sitting, sinking, or going to the ground. Do not imply impact, injury, or an opponent.
